aspect: Blast produces mixed hearing loss, not simple acoustic trauma
description: Both conductive and sensorineural components, which distinguishes it from occupational noise damage and means it responds differently to treatment.
energy_note: A different injury with the same name.

aspect: A clean hearing test that does not clear you
description: Research found objective speech-recognition performance predicted by TBI status while subjective hearing complaints were predicted by blast exposure - people with blast history have communication deficits beyond what standard audiometry predicts.
energy_note: Tested normal, and still cannot follow a conversation.

aspect: Sudden-onset tinnitus is worse than gradual
description: Tinnitus from blast may be more detrimental than occupational tinnitus precisely because it appears instantly rather than creeping in - there is no period of adaptation and no forewarning.
energy_note: A noise that starts on a Tuesday and never stops.

aspect: Civilians have none of the preparation
description: Soldiers have hearing protection, a baseline audiogram and an occupational health pathway. Civilians under bombardment have none of the three, and no record of what their hearing was before.

aspect: SECONDARY - it takes the social life first
description: Restaurants, gatherings, group conversation. Withdrawal is the standard adaptation, and it is indistinguishable from depression to everyone watching.
energy_note: Stopped going out, and everyone assumed it was sadness.

description: Speech recognition in a second language is already harder. Doing it with blast-injured auditory processing in a noisy office is a compound disability that no assessment measures.
energy_note: Two deficits that multiply instead of adding.
notes: Direct interaction with the language and workplace hurdles in assets/text/iran.
